cases.name: self_reported_success
cases.threat: a receipt claims outcome completed and a perfect score the evidence never earned

cases.name: duplicate_reward_key_reuse
cases.threat: the same operation key commits the same delivery twice (broken ledger idempotency)

cases.name: teleport_illegal_transition
cases.threat: a claimed committed pick the robot never could perform from its true position

cases.name: trace_final_mismatch
cases.threat: final_state.json is swapped and the run_finished binding is reforged to match

cases.name: budget_bypass
cases.threat: a committed operation claims policy step 101 beyond the locked budget

cases.name: unauthorized_effect
cases.threat: a committed place effect without a place grant

cases.name: seed_config_substitution
cases.threat: config and replay identity claim a different seed than the task evidence

cases.name: idempotency_failure
cases.threat: a resubmission of a stored key+payload is recorded as a fresh rejection instead of the ledger replay

cases.name: artifact_substitution
cases.threat: task.json is substituted with another seed's task

cases.name: partial_credit_gaming
cases.threat: a receipt inflates verified_score above the independently recomputed floor score

description: Frozen named reward-hacking fixtures (REQ-06, T-21). Each case names one mandatory adversarial tamper vector against the verifier and the exact expected VerificationResult shape: valid, outcome, and the signature violation codes that MUST appear. The tamper builders live in tests/test_adversarial_verifier.py and forge hand-built artifact mappings only (no Runner, ToolBay, or policy object is ever constructed).
